problem: A store manager is choosing $3$ employees to do the morning, afternoon, and night shifts. If the store has $9$ employees and each can work a single shift, how many ways of choosing the $3$ employees does the manager have?

feedback.worked_solution:
The formula for ${}_{n}{P}_{r}$ is given by

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}\,.
$$

$P(5,3)$ means the same thing as ${}_{5}{P}_{3}.$ Using the usual formula for ${}_{n}{P}_{r},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(5,3) & =\frac{5!}{(5-3)!} \\  & =\frac{5!}{2!} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot \cancel{2!}}{\cancel{2!}} \\  & =5\cdot 4\cdot 3 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$
